primitives.name: Risk-adjusted Wage Approximation
primitives.verbatim_quote: 302 RISK, UNCERTAINTY, AND PROFIT and the like, so that the wages of labor are in fact generally a fair approximation to a guaranteed contractual return.
primitives.assumptions: Labor contracts are treated as quasi-fixed returns; risk is effectively transferred via market mechanisms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when labor loses contractual protection, reverting to pure variable returns.

primitives.name: Classical Profit Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: As observed in our historical introduction (chapter π) the older English economists used the term "profit" to designate the income of the owner of a business, who was regarded as essentially an investor.
primitives.assumptions: Historically, profit was treated as residual income after capital costs; interest and profit were not distinguished.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs during financial crises when debt service consumes all residual earnings.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Residual valuation models; GSE: Debt-service coverage ratios.

primitives.name: Interest-Profit Distinction Relocation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Little was made of the latter as constituting a distinction between profit and interest, as ordinary contract interest so obviously contains an element of payment for risk also.
primitives.assumptions: Both interest and profit contain risk compensation; the distinction is blurred under standard contract theory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown happens when risk-free rates approach zero, collapsing the spread between safe and risky assets.

layer2.telemetry: Credit spreads relative to short-term rates

The four primitives formalize the core economic insight that risk, control, and returns are mathematically interconvertible under standard market equilibrium. The "risk-adjusted wage approximation" shows how labor contracts can replicate capital returns through insurance-like mechanisms. The "classical profit classification" highlights the historical unity of entrepreneurial income before modern finance disaggregated it into interest and profit. The "interest-profit distinction relocation" demonstrates that both are forms of risk compensation, undermining traditional dichotomies. Finally, the "effective control-risk equivalence" establishes that bearing uncertainty is functionally identical to exercising operational discretion, justifying their unified treatment. These operators map directly to GSI's Bayesian inference frameworks for pricing kernels and to GSE's state-transition models for governance dynamics, providing a rigorous foundation for understanding economic agency.
